s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic swelling and pain in the mastoid area with a calcified mass
salient_findings: Pain and swelling in the right mastoid area
Hyperostotic lesion of the outer table of the right calvarium
Densely calcified mass involving the inferior squamosal portion of the right temporal bone
key_facts: 28-year-old man with a history of migraine disorder
Several months of pain and swelling in the right mastoid area
Recent subjective enlargement of the mass and increased pain
Noncontrast CT showed a 3.0 × 3.0 × 1.1 cm hyperostotic lesion
MRI revealed a densely calcified mass measuring 3.6 × 1.5 × 3.0 cm
Low signal intensity on T1- and T2-weighted images
Mild patchy internal enhancement
Thickening of the inner table
No soft-tissue component beyond the bone or dural involvement
Laboratory studies were within normal limits

shortlist.label: Osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperostotic lesion with calcified mass and low signal intensity on T1- and T2-weighted images

shortlist.label: Osteoblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Densely calcified mass with mild patchy internal enhancement and thickening of the inner table

shortlist.label: Mastoid osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Location-specific diagnosis matching the patient's symptoms and imaging findings

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of hyperostotic lesion and calcified mass, although less likely given the patient's age and lack of other symptoms

shortlist.label: Ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of calcified mass and hyperostotic lesion, with a similar appearance on imaging studies

raw.rationale: The presence of a hyperostotic lesion with dense calcification and low signal intensity on T1- and T2-weighted images, along with mild patchy internal enhancement, is consistent with an osteoma. The lack of soft-tissue component or dural involvement also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Osteoblastoma
rejected.why: Osteoblastomas are typically larger and more aggressive than the described lesion, and often have a softer tissue component.

rejected.label: Mastoid osteoma
rejected.why: While the location is consistent, the term 'mastoid osteoma' is not a standard diagnosis and 'osteoma' is a more general and appropriate term for this type of lesion.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Fibrous dysplasia typically has a ground-glass appearance on imaging and may have a more complex appearance than the described lesion.

rejected.label: Ossifying fibroma
rejected.why: Ossifying fibromas are typically found in the jaw and have a distinct appearance with a fibrous component, which is not described in this case.
